issues.x: Owners describe heavy oil use (one reports over 1 quart per 1,000 miles) and sudden engine failures in NHTSA complaints, including a 2019 engine that locked up at 450 miles. We found no Ford recall or bulletin for it.

issues.t: Oil leaks at the filter and cooler
issues.rx: oil filter|oil leak|leaking oil|oil cooler|oil pressure sensor
issues.x: Ford bulletins cover leaks from damaged oil cooler tube O-rings (2015–2018) and from the oil pressure sensor near the filter (2017 cars built Jan–Sep 2017). Ford also sent 2015–2017 owners a free oil filter wrench, and some owners report filters coming loose.
issues.fix: Replace the cooler tube O-rings (SSM 47364) or follow TSB 18-2159.

issues.x: On 2016–2017 cars a rattle at light throttle when cold comes from piston motion in the bore. Ford says it fades when warm and is not a durability concern.
Ford bulletins describe hesitation or surging with no fault codes on 2015–2020 GT350 and GT350R, sometimes with cruise control not working.
issues.fix: Ford TSB 22-2140, the latest version, gives the service procedure.

issues.x: On some 2020 GT350 and GT500 5.2L engines the secondary timing chain tensioner may not have been activated at assembly. That can cause timing loss, misfires and engine damage.
issues.fix: Dealers inspect the tensioner free under Ford program 21B26.

issues.x: A class action said 2016 Base and Technology cars, sold without transmission and differential coolers, overheat and go into limp mode. A Florida jury found for Ford in March 2024, and the two sides then agreed to settle.
issues.fix: The coolers are standard on every GT350 from 2017.
